title: Towards End-to-End Multi-Object Visual Tracking: A Survey and Outlook
content: Multi-object visual tracking (MOT) is a fundamental computer vision task focused on locating multiple objects within a video sequence and maintaining their unique identities over time. Traditional approaches often decompose this problem into separate steps: object detection, feature extraction, data association, etc. While effective, this fragmented pipeline can accumulate errors and requires careful tuning of each independent component and often leads to high computational demand. A transformative trend in recent literature is the shift towards joint and end-to-end MOT that integrates detection and other components into a possibly single, unified learning process. This paradigm formulates MOT by leveraging modern deep learning architectures to simultaneously reason about object locations and their identities across frames. This review critically analyzes the rapid development of these joint and end-to-end trackers, highlighting their promise in simplifying training pipelines and achieving state-of-the-art performance through joint optimization. We synthesize the core principles of this approach, identify persistent challenges such as occlusion handling and computational demands, and discuss promising future research directions, providing a structured overview of the evolving joint and end-to-end MOT landscape along with a summary of datasets and evaluation metrics for performance evaluation of MOT methods.
